headline: Congress repealed a 1948 law that had given the State of Iowa criminal jurisdiction over certain offenses on the Sac and Fox Indian Reservation.
what_it_does: A 1948 act had given the State of Iowa authority to handle criminal offenses committed by or against Indians on the Sac and Fox Indian Reservation. This law cancels that 1948 act, so it no longer applies. The official summary does not say how jurisdiction on the reservation is handled after the repeal.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Sac and Fox Nation and other Native Americans living on the Sac and Fox Indian Reservation
who_it_affects.how: The state of Iowa no longer has the jurisdiction the 1948 act gave it over offenses involving Indians on the reservation.

who_it_affects.group: Iowa state courts and law enforcement agencies that work near the Sac and Fox Indian Reservation
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have the authority under the repealed 1948 act to handle certain criminal cases on the reservation.

when_it_takes_effect: It became law on December 11, 2018, when it was enacted.
